decisions.why: The psalm's first word of address. *Púer* is first a child (L&S: 'orig. a child, whether boy or girl'), and also a servant; the Greek παῖδες holds both senses; the Hebrew has 'servants of the LORD' (עַבְדֵי), which the CNBB Liturgia das Horas and Lecionário follow (*ó servos do Senhor*, verified, liturgy-br/ps112.txt), as do MS1932 (*vós, seus servos*) and DM1962. Rule 1: the Hebrew does not decide the Latin's sense. The Latin Church plainly hears children in this verse: DO sets *Laudáte, púeri, Dóminum* as the Alleluia of the Holy Innocents (missa Sancti/12-28), and in the Masses of St John Bosco (01-31), St Thérèse of the Child Jesus (10-03), the Seven Holy Brothers with their mother (07-10, joined to 112:9), and Easter Saturday for the neophytes (Pasc0-6) — grep. Douay-Rheims: *ye children*. The glossary row *púer → servo* (open, Ps 68:18, 85:16) is for *púer tuus*, a servant of God addressed to God, where a possessive makes the servant sense; here the vocative plural stands bare. Ruled *meninos*: the Latin's first sense and its liturgy's; *servos* kept as option 1 and **flagged for Gustavo** — it is the line Brazil knows.

options.label: meninos
options.note: Ruling. DRB 'ye children'; the Latin liturgy's reading (Holy Innocents, Bosco, Thérèse, Easter Saturday). Masculine plural as the generic 'children'.

options.label: servos
options.note: The glossary row púer → servo (for púer tuus); MS1932 'vós, seus servos'; the CNBB 'ó servos do Senhor' (from the Hebrew) — the familiar line. Closes the Latin's ambiguity the other way.

options.label: crianças
options.note: Gender-neutral as *púer* 'boy or girl' is; heard as small children only, and of a catechism register.

decisions.why: DO's Latin carries the rubric *(fit reverentia)* inside the verse, at the Name (a bow). The glossary row (Ps 67:5a; also 110:9b) keeps it translated in parentheses and asks Gustavo whether rubrics are kept or dropped. Followed as the row stands; it is not prayed aloud (the checks strip parentheses).

options.label: (faz-se reverência)
options.note: Ruling: the row, as 67:5a and 110:9b.

options.label: (dropped)
options.note: No rubric in the prayed text; the Latin column keeps it.

decisions.why: A formula said alone as a versicle (DO: *V. Sit nomen Dómini benedíctum*, several offices; the antiphon *Sit nomen Dómini * benedíctum in sǽcula*) and, in Brazil, the opening of the CNBB Liturgia das Horas verse: *Bendito seja o nome do Senhor* (verified). The words are the Latin's one for one (*sit* → *seja*, *benedíctum* → *bendito*, the benedícere row); only the order is at stake, and D2 lets natural order lead. The adjective-first order is how Portuguese says a wish of blessing (cf. the settled *Bendito o Senhor*, D41) and is the line the ear already has.

forms.sitnomen: Bendito seja o nome do Senhor

decisions.latin: ex hoc nunc, et usque in sǽculum
decisions.why: *Usque in sǽculum* is D37's formula (*para todo o sempre*; the row lists 112:2). *Ex hoc nunc* ('from this now') is new to the glossary (it returns at 113:18, 120:8, 124:2b, 130:3 — grep): *desde agora* keeps the 'from' (*ex*) the Latin names and that MS1932 and DRB ('from henceforth now') keep; the CNBB's *agora e por toda a eternidade* drops it and spends *eternidade*. The Latin's *et* kept. The bishop's blessing dialogue is reported as *Agora e para sempre* — seen only in a search summary, not fetched: unverified, and it drops *ex* and *usque* both.

options.label: desde agora e para todo o sempre

forms.exhoc: desde agora e para todo o sempre

options.note: Ruling; D37 for *usque in sǽculum*; *ex hoc nunc → desde agora* (new row).

options.label: desde agora e para sempre
options.note: MS1932; the bare D23 form — drops *usque*, against D37.

options.label: agora e por toda a eternidade

forms.exhoc: agora e por toda a eternidade

options.note: CNBB Liturgia das Horas (from the Hebrew; verified). Refused: drops *ex*, and *eternidade* is not the *sǽculum* rows' word.

decisions.why: The first colon copies the settled formula of 49:1b (*Desde o nascer do sol até o poente*, D44; the row says 112:3 should copy it). The Latin has an adjective, *laudábile*, where the Greek has the imperative αἰνεῖτε and the Hebrew a participle (CNBB *louvado seja*): the Latin is followed. *Digno de louvor* is the settled rendering of *laudábilis* (47:2 formula *muito digno de louvor*). The Latin is a nominal sentence; a copula is supplied (D2), as MS1932 does. The colon runs +3 syllables on the Latin's 9 — accepted: the formula's words cannot be shortened, and the copula makes it a sentence. The colon ends on *nome do Senhor* as 112:1b does, as the Latin does.

options.label: é digno de louvor
options.note: Ruling; copula supplied; MS1932 'é digno de louvor o nome do Senhor'.

options.label: digno de louvor
options.note: The Latin's nominal sentence kept, as *Bendito o Senhor* (D41); after a long adverbial first colon it may be heard as a fragment.

options.label: louvável
options.note: The cognate adjective, shorter (fits the Latin's length); in Brazil *louvável* is 'commendable', as of an initiative — too slight for the Name.

decisions.why: Words by the rows: *excélsus → excelso* (D43), *gentes → nações*, *super → sobre* (the *super* (place) row; 98:2 *excelso sobre todos os povos*). The Latin frames the colon *Excélsus … Dóminus*; the ruling keeps *Excelso* first and moves the subject up with its copula, the natural order (D2), as MS1932 does. This colon is also said alone as a versicle (DO, Major Special: *V. Excélsus super omnes gentes Dóminus*).

options.label: Excelso é o Senhor sobre todas as nações

options.note: The Latin's frame, with the subject last.

forms.excelsus: O Senhor é excelso sobre todas as nações

options.note: Plain prose order (cf. 98:2 in its second colon); loses the Latin's first word.

decisions.why: The Latin has no verb; Portuguese needs one (D2). *Quem é como* is the plain question and DM1962's; MS1932 has *Quem há como*, which asks whether any exists.

options.label: Quem é como
options.note: Ruling; DM1962 diction.

decisions.latin: et humília réspicit in cælo et in terra
decisions.why: *Humília* is a neuter plural (τὰ ταπεινά): lowly things, not lowly people. DRB 'the low things'; MS1932 glosses 'as criaturas humildes'. *O que é humilde* keeps the neuter and the *húmilis → humilde* row (D27) in one plain clause; *os humildes* would make it persons. *Réspicere → olhar para*, as in the finished 103:32 *Ele, que olha para a terra*, 30:8, 32:14 (the glossary row is open; *estar voltado para* is for eyes, 10:5b). *In cælo et in terra* is left at the end, where the Latin has it, so that it may go with *réspicit* or with both verbs, as the Latin allows.

options.label: olha para o que é humilde

forms.humilia: olha para o que é humilde

options.note: Ruling; the neuter as a clause.

options.label: olha para as coisas humildes
options.note: DRB 'the low things'; the neuter as a noun; *coisas* is flat.

options.label: olha para os humildes
options.note: Makes it persons (MS1932's gloss); closes what the neuter leaves wide.

decisions.why: Two participles hanging on *Dóminus* of 112:5, with no main verb. The gerund keeps the Latin's build, as the finished 17:51 *Engrandecendo as salvações do seu Rei* does (magnificáre row: 'the participle as a gerund, dangling as the Latin's does'). *Suscitáre* here is to lift up (L&S); the cognate *suscitar* in Brazil means 'to provoke, arouse' (77:5 *suscitou um testemunho* is a different sense), so *levantar*; *érigere → erguer* (the row, 19:9). The CNBB and DM1962 make finite verbs (*Levanta*).

options.label: Levantando … erguendo
options.note: Ruling; the Latin's participles as gerunds.

options.label: Ele levanta … ergue
options.note: Finite verbs (DM1962, CNBB 'Levanta'); plainer, but makes a new sentence the Latin does not have.

options.label: Suscitando … erguendo
options.note: The cognate; heard as 'provoking'.

decisions.why: Concrete images stay concrete (rule 5): *stercus* is dung. *Esterco* is the plain Brazilian word for it. MS1932 *da imundície* abstracts; the CNBB *do lixo* changes the thing; DM1962 *do monturo* (dunghill) is exact but a word many will not know.

options.label: do esterco
options.note: Ruling.

options.label: do monturo
options.note: DM1962; the dunghill; less current.

options.label: da imundície
options.note: MS1932; the image softened.

decisions.why: *Qui* continues the chain begun at *Dóminus* (112:5), across the gerunds and the purpose clause. A bare *Que* at the head of a verse is heard as 'that' or as an exclamation; the pronoun is named, as the finished 103:32 does (*Ele, que olha para a terra*). *Habitáre facit → faz habitar*, as 28:10 and 67:6b (*Deus, que faz habitar numa casa…*), whose Latin is nearly this colon's; the verse keeps the echo with 112:5 *hábitat → habita*.

options.label: Ele, que faz habitar
options.note: Ruling; = 103:32's build.

options.label: Que faz habitar
options.note: The bare relative, as the Latin.

options.label: Ele faz habitar
options.note: A main verb; drops the relative.

decisions.why: No possessive in the Latin (οἴκῳ). *Numa casa*, as 67:6b *faz habitar numa casa* (*inhabitáre facit … in domo*). MS1932 and the CNBB add *sua*.

options.label: numa casa
options.note: Ruling; = 67:6b.

options.label: na sua casa
options.note: MS1932 'em sua casa'; supplies a possessive.

decisions.why: In apposition to *stérilem*: the barren one dwells as a mother of sons, rejoicing; *lætántem* agrees with *matrem*, not *filiórum*. The adjective *alegre* is the plainer of two faithful words for the participle (D2) and cannot be read with *filhos*; *que se alegra* after *filhos* could. DM1962 *mãe alegre de filhos* puts it between noun and complement. The colon runs 2 syllables short of the Latin — accepted.

options.label: alegre mãe de filhos
options.note: Ruling.

options.label: mãe alegre de filhos
options.note: DM1962's order.

options.label: mãe de filhos, que se alegra

forms.matrem: mãe de filhos, que se alegra

options.note: Keeps the verb of the participle (*lætári → alegrar-se*); the relative can be misattached to *filhos* by the ear.

choices.112:1: *laudáre → louvar* (D5 keeps it apart from *confitéri → dar graças*); *Louvai* is safe at the *vós* imperative (past *louvei*). The echo *Senhor … Senhor* at mediant and final is the Latin's own (*Dóminum … Dómini*). Plural humans → *vós* (decided).
choices.112:2: Second colon flagged +3 by the counter, which does not elide: said aloud, *desde‿agora‿e para todo‿o sempre* is 10 syllables, the Latin's count. Accepted.
choices.112:3: First colon = 49:1b word for word (the formula row, D44).
choices.112:4: *et super cælos glória ejus → e sobre os céus a sua glória*: the ellipsis of the verb kept, as 56:6 *e por toda a terra a vossa glória*.
choices.112:5: *in altis → nas alturas*, as 92:4b. DO's inline *(6)* is not reproduced.
choices.112:7: *inops → carente* (D38), *pauper → pobre*. The Latin pairs them; kept apart.
choices.112:8: *collocáre → colocar* (row open; 22:1). The Latin's anadiplosis *cum princípibus, cum princípibus* kept whole. *príncipes* is proparoxytone before the asterisk — the Latin's *princípibus* is too, and the repetition forbids any other word; accepted. *princeps → príncipe* as 81:7, 117:9 (the CNBB's *nobres* is not taken).

audit.note: Psalm-level draft from consult/parallels/ps112.md (Latin, LXX, Hebrew, DRB, MS1932, DM1962). Rows applied: D5 (laudáre stays *louvar*), D37 *para todo o sempre*, D44 formula *Desde o nascer do sol até o poente*, *laudábilis → digno de louvor* (47:2), D43 *excelso*, *gentes → nações*, *super → sobre*, D27 *humilde*, D38 *carente*, *érigere → erguer*, *collocáre → colocar*, *habitáre facit → faz habitar* (28:10, 67:6b), the *(fit reverentia)* row. New: *púeri* (vocative, bare) → *meninos* against the *púer → servo* row, which is for *púer tuus* (decision `pueri`, flagged); *ex hoc nunc → desde agora*. Brazilian liturgical circulation checked by fetch (ps112/liturgy-br/ps112.txt): the CNBB Liturgia das Horas Sl 112(113) (*Louvai, louvai, ó servos do Senhor … Bendito seja o nome do Senhor, agora e por toda a eternidade!*) and the Lecionário refrain *Louvai o Senhor, que eleva os pobres!* (25th Sunday, year C) — both from the Hebrew; used only to see what the ear knows. The bishop's-blessing dialogue *Bendito seja o nome do Senhor. — Agora e para sempre* is reported in a search summary only, unverified.

Hard checks pass (exit 0). Soft: 112:1 rhyme *Senhor … Senhor* — the Latin's own echo (*Dóminum … Dómini*), kept; 112:2b +3 — the counter does not elide, 10 when said; 112:3b +3 — the settled *digno de louvor* plus a copula, accepted (decision `laudabile`); 112:8a proparoxytone *príncipes* before the asterisk — the Latin's *princípibus* too, the repetition forbids another word.
